newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian shares retreat with Europe, rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares retreat with Europe, rate rise.

text.p: Norwegian shares traded down on Wednesday following the course of Wall Street and other major European bourses.
Dealers said the market was nervous ahead of a batch of U.S. economic data and a rise in domestic interest rates following a weakening of the crown.
Oslo's Total share index closed 1.26 percent off at 1307.44 crowns in hefty turnover of 1.3 billion crowns.
"Most of the blue chips went down today and the rise in interest rates is putting pressure on the technology sector," said one broker.
The Oslo-traded share of Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) jumped 8.6 percent after the company beat market expectations for the second quarter.

SAS said increased volumes and lower costs boosted second quarter operating profits before writeoffs by 32 percent to 1.76 billion Swedish crowns. Pre-tax profit amounted to 1.38 billion crowns, more than double analysts' forecasts.

Anglo-Norwegian Kvaerner ASA slipped 0.21 percent to 478 crowns in a slight correction after recent sttep gains. The outlook for the company remains bullish with eight out of 10 analysts polled by Reuters recommending to buy the share.
